content.value_statement: Backend systems become hard to test when business logic mixes with frameworks. This skill guides practical architecture choices using Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and DDD.
actual_capabilities: Explains Clean Architecture layers and inward dependency rules.
Provides a Python Clean Architecture directory structure and examples.
Shows ports and adapters for payment, notification, and repository boundaries.
Demonstrates DDD value objects, entities, aggregates, and domain events.
Lists best practices and common pitfalls for backend architecture work.
limitations: Focuses on backend architecture, not frontend application structure.
Examples are illustrative Python snippets, not a complete runnable project.
Does not generate database migrations, deployment scripts, or production configuration.
Requires domain context before choosing boundaries and patterns.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Backend Service
use_cases.description: Choose layers, ports, adapters, and domain boundaries before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Coupled Application
use_cases.description: Separate business rules from frameworks, databases, and controllers in planned steps.

use_cases.title: Define Team Architecture Standards
use_cases.description: Create shared rules for modules, repositories, use cases, and domain models.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and DDD for this backend: [describe domain, team size, data stores, and integrations].

prompt_templates.title: Map Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Map bounded contexts, core entities, repositories, and use cases for this product area: [describe workflows, users, and business rules].

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Gradually
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased refactoring plan that moves this coupled backend toward ports and adapters: [describe current modules and pain points].

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Fitness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backend architecture for dependency direction, domain purity, testability, and over-engineering risk: [summarize modules and dependencies].

output_examples.input: A team needs to design an order service with payments and notifications.
output: Recommended pattern: Hexagonal Architecture with domain services at the core.
Ports: order repository, payment gateway, and notification sender.
Validation: domain tests should run without Stripe, email, or database dependencies.

output_examples.input: A controller contains validation, persistence calls, and email sending.
output: Refactor direction: move business rules into a use case.
Keep the controller responsible only for HTTP input and response mapping.
Introduce repository and notification interfaces before changing infrastructure code.

output_examples.input: A product team wants DDD for customer and order workflows.
output: Start with bounded contexts for customer profile, ordering, and payment.
Model aggregates around consistency needs, not database table names.
Use domain events for completed orders and payment outcomes.

best_practices: Start with domain boundaries before choosing folders and frameworks.
Keep dependencies pointing toward the domain core.
Validate designs with tests that replace databases and external services.
anti_patterns: Putting business rules inside controllers or framework handlers.
Creating abstractions before the domain has real complexity.
Letting ORM models leak into use cases and domain entities.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when backend maintainability, testing, or module boundaries are the main design problem.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples that need adaptation to your stack.

faq.question: Can it help with existing monoliths?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline phased refactors that isolate use cases and infrastructure dependencies.

faq.question: Which patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and tactical Domain-Driven Design patterns.

faq.question: Does it require Python?
faq.answer: No. The examples use Python, but the architecture concepts apply to many backend languages.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
